[h1] Review [/h1]
Visual Novel of the Nukige genre that serves as a sequel to kuroinu, continuing the story of revenge and cruel devastation of the first installment but after a few years and with new characters and an artistic section with more modern designs but keeping the rawness of the scenes accompanied by high sexual content.
The story of the game focuses on the invasion of the towns by Derek Rondo in a dark fantasy world with elves, witches, dwarves, etc. And how this with his army is devastating places, killing the villagers and submitting as sex toys to female characters either for personal use or as a reward to motivate his army or to bribe high commanders, the game as such does not have a really deep story since being a Nukige focuses only on giving excuses to meet new female characters to later have scenes of sexual type with them.
Most of the story of the game is linear [spoiler] until you get to know the 9 main girls [/spoiler] from there the game lets you choose one of the girls to advance in their story and get their scenes and then their end, since it does not let you continue with the other stories once you finish one, you have to have a save with this choice so you can see all the endings of each girl.
The game also has small bonus stories, such as alternative scenes of the girls of this installment but also with a small compilation of some of the events that occurred in the first installment, which gladly extends the duration of the title.
As for the graphical aspect gives a great leap in quality, offering a more modern character design and costumes more lewd, plus more elaborate and detailed backgrounds. On the part of the sound section maintains the good level of the last installment with excellent voice acting for all characters with a tone of voice appropriate for the personality of each character and good interpretation of emotions.

💭[b]Conclusion[/b]
A highly recommended nukige for lovers of dark fantasy with elves, dark elves, priestesses, witches and different kinds of girls that will certainly satisfy your personal desires, the game is also the most complete version to include all possible content with even the bonus scenarios and the recapitulation of the previous game, on the part of the story there is really nothing remarkable as it ends up being quite generic with the abuse of power main plot and the only decision to take to decide which end to see first.
The price is somewhat higher than most of Shiravune's visual novels but given the quantity and quality of content is acceptable but if you want to get more out of quality price, I recommend you buy it with the release discount or a later season at the price of 20 dollars.

An overall solid and DARK VN and decent localization from Shiravune.  This fits firmly in their Dark Dreamers bundle so if you like your stories happy and romance light, you want to avoid this.  External update is gonna be very important to get most the story and content.  The art is fantastic.  It's all stills and in Shiravune localization fashion is still kept in their original JP form, but between the extensive story and the additional append content a whopping 101 scenes with a myriad of changes to progress along with the verbose but not overly wordy storytelling.  There is only one choice about halfway through the main story that you'll want to make a save at to be more efficient in visiting all routes, though for the extra impatient there is an unlock all option as well.  The translation work is decent and while there's the occasional typo, pronoun mistake, and redundancy it doesn't reek of machine translation poetry or a complete lack of quality control. Music is good and the voice acting is excellent, every line by the female cast is recorded which is impressive with it not being a few hour speed read.  Overall an excellent entry in Shiravune's ever-expanding library of iconic VNs localized.

[h1][b][1] Intro : [/b][/h1]

In the world of visual novels, Kuroinu 2 Redux emerges as a fascinating and complex narrative, diving deep into themes of lust, power, and betrayal. Set in the decadent land of Negramstia, this game offers a unique experience that can both captivate and leave players divided. Let's explore what users are saying about it and dissect the game's strengths and weaknesses.

[h1][b][2] Game Experience : [/b][/h1]

At its core, Kuroinu 2 Redux weaves a tale of a corrupt and prosperous nation, ruled by the enchanting yet ruthless Empress Ladomira. This dark narrative sets the stage for a Holy Alliance's uprising, united against the empire's tyranny. As the player, you embody Derek Rondo, a character rumored to be the reincarnation of the legendary Mercenary King Vult. While he successfully defends the nation, his hidden ambition to seize the throne unfolds as the central plot, promising a complex and intriguing story.

One of the game's standout features is its full Japanese voice acting by seasoned professionals, which adds depth and authenticity to the characters. The characters themselves are diverse and intricate, each with their unique backgrounds and motivations, contributing to the game's complex narrative.

However, despite its compelling narrative and character development, Kuroinu 2 Redux is not without its drawbacks. Some players have expressed disappointment in the lack of sound, especially given the game's full-price tag. While the erotic scenes are visually stunning, there's a sense of repetitiveness and limited variation, which might leave players wanting more.

Furthermore, the game boasts a considerable number of characters, but the overall quantity of CG images and variations falls short compared to other games in the same genre. This might be seen as a missed opportunity to fully immerse players in the story.

On the positive side, some players commend the game for its wide array of situations and patterns, keeping them engaged and intrigued. They also note improvements compared to the previous installment in the series, making Kuroinu 2 Redux a worthwhile addition for fans.

However, the darker and more brutal aspects of the narrative can be disheartening for some players, as it goes beyond the boundaries of traditional storytelling. The shattered promises and compromised morals of the protagonist may not resonate with those seeking a more coherent and rational narrative.

[h1][b][3] Verdict : [/b][/h1]

In conclusion, Kuroinu 2 Redux is a complex visual novel that pushes the boundaries of storytelling, presenting a dark and ambitious narrative. While it excels in character development and offers a wide array of situations, it falls short in some aspects, such as the lack of sound and limited variation in erotic scenes. The game's departure from traditional storytelling may be a point of contention for some players. Nevertheless, if you're a fan of intricate narratives and don't shy away from the darker aspects of storytelling, Kuroinu 2 Redux is a game worth considering. Just be aware that the Steam version requires an external patch for R18+ content, which may be somewhat inconvenient for some players.
